observation.visible_scene: A bartender in a dark suit with a magenta pocket square stands behind a bar, holding a stainless-steel shaker cup tilted over a coupe glass that contains a single large clear ice sphere. A thin stream of reddish-amber liquid pours from the lip of the shaker into the glass. Several glass bottles with metal pour spouts sit on the counter in the foreground (left and right), and a softly blurred wall of bottles forms the background.
visible_changes: The shaker cup gradually rotates/tilts downward across the segment, its opening pointing more steeply toward the glass by the last frame than in the first, consistent with the hand lowering the vessel as it empties.
A continuous thin stream of liquid flows from the shaker into the glass throughout the excerpt; it is already in progress at t=0 and still running at t=3.33s.
The liquid level in the coupe glass appears to rise slightly around the base of the ice sphere from the first to the last frame.
The pouring hand and forearm shift position subtly along with the tilting shaker, while the bartender's torso and head remain essentially still.
The coupe glass, ice sphere, foreground bottles, and background shelving hold their positions relative to the frame, indicating a static camera with no noticeable pan or zoom.
outside_clip_unknowns: The beginning of the pour (the segment starts mid-pour) and its completion or stop.
What liquid is being poured and the final drink composition.
The bartender's face and the contents remaining in the shaker.
Any action before t=0 or after t=3.33s.
uncertain_details: The exact magnitude of the liquid-level rise is small and partly inferred from lighting on the glass.
Whether the ice sphere rotates or shifts slightly from the incoming stream is not clearly resolvable.
Any very minor camera drift cannot be fully separated from the static background evidence.
